title: Adaptive tenant guardrails and contracted throughput enforcement
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Some Dedicated customers require signed throughput guarantees for committed capacity, while we need stronger noisy-neighbor mitigation that preserves tail-latency SLOs. Current soft quota/scarcity controls are reactive (eviction after high GPU utilization) and lack a predictable, contract-aware enforcement path. This ticket implements an adaptive guardrail layer that maps per-customer contracted throughput to dynamic allocation signals, provides soft reclaimable credits for bursty workloads, and integrates with the autoscaling controller to maintain throughput guarantees with graceful degradation for low-priority tenants. Goals: 1) Enforce contracted throughput for committed capacity while allowing controlled bursts; 2) Reduce p99 token latency regressions caused by cross-tenant interference; 3) Provide observability (exposed metrics and dashboards) and a clear escalation path for ops and account teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New admission controller enforces per-tenant committed throughput at the request-routing layer, returning clear 429 variants when limits would break guaranteed SLOs. 2) Soft-credit engine issues reclaimable burst credits per tenant (configurable by contract) and enforces preemption rules when credits depleted. 3) Autoscaler uses tenant-level signals (contracted_throughput, current_consumption, queued_requests, credit_balance) to scale pools; documented behavior for canary & emergency scale-ups. 4) Observability: dashboards showing per-tenant throughput, credit usage, p50/p95/p99 latency, and allocation decisions; alerting rules for sustained SLO risk. 5) Runbook and pilot with two internal customers; no regressions in cluster stability under synthetic noisy-neighbor tests.
design_notes: Architecture: (a) Admission controller: lightweight pre-check at the router that consults a fast in-memory tenancy store + credit ledger. (b) Credit ledger: per-tenant token bucket implemented in the runtime control plane with epoched reconciliation to the canonical DB to tolerate leader churn. (c) Autoscaler integration: extend the existing dedicated autoscaler to accept a ContractedThroughput target plus a RiskScore calculated from credit burn rate and queue lengths. (d) Preemption policy: low-priority preemptible placements are marked and can be evicted within a configured reclaim window; preemption events are recorded as traceable events for billing/incident analysis. Edge cases/trade-offs: strong enforcement adds request-level rejections that may impact UX; we mitigate via staged rollouts, informative error payloads, and customer-facing quota dashboards. We instrument SM/PCIe utilization and model-token throughput (tokens/s on GPU) for better signal fidelity.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary) - internal tenants only: enable admission controller with soft mode (audit-only) for two weeks; monitor false positives. Phase 2 (pilot) - selected external customers: enable enforcement for non-critical contracts with credits enabled; runbook for account team. Phase 3 - general availability: enforcement + autoscaler integration + dashboards; enable configurable contract fields for sales. Rollback: feature flag to revert to legacy soft-quota behavior, and emergency throttle mode to prefer graceful degradation over hard rejections.
metrics: Per-tenant: contracted_throughput_rps, observed_rps, credit_balance, credit_burn_rate, admission_denials (count & reasons), p50/p95/p99 latency (tokens), queue_length, scale_actions (timestamped). SLO rules: maintain contracted_throughput availability >= 99.9% over 1h windows; p99 latency degradation from baseline < 20% when within contracted allocation.
test_plan: Unit tests for token bucket correctness and reconcile when leader fails. Integration tests: simulate mixed tenants (guaranteed vs best-effort) with synthetic models to measure latency p99 under increasing load. Chaos test: kill router leader and verify ledger reconciliation preserves credits. Load test: saturate GPU pools to verify preemption rules and autoscaler triggers expected scale actions. QA checklist includes observability validation, billing signal sanity checks, and customer-facing error message verification.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive preemption could cause customer-visible failures for best-effort tenants. Mitigation: default to soft-preempt for first 24h and auto-escalate only when contracted tenant SLOs are at risk. Risk: inaccurate throughput signal due to model-level token variability. Mitigation: instrument per-model tokens/s and allow per-model weight overrides in contract mapping.

notes_for_ops: Ops runbook: 1) Feature flags: dedicated.contract_throughput.enforce, dedicated.credit_ledger.leader. 2) On 429 spikes, check credit_burn_rate and ledger reconciliation logs; consider temporarily increasing burst window for affected tenant. 3) If autoscaler misfires, toggle autoscaler.risk_score.penalty to revert decisions. Logging: ensure admission decisions log tenant, reason, request_id, and current credit_balance.
